author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function strips the **outermost pair of parentheses** from every top-level group in a valid parentheses string. It walks through the string one character at a time while tracking a `level` counter that represents how deeply nested the current position is. The order of the three checks is the clever part: when it sees a `)` it **decrements** `level` *before* deciding whether to keep the character, and when it sees a `(` it **increments** `level` *after* that decision. This means an opening parenthesis is only appended to `res` if we were already inside a group (`level > 0`) before it appeared, and a closing parenthesis is only kept if a group is still open after it closes. The outermost `(` of each group arrives at `level === 0` and the outermost `)` brings `level` back to `0`, so both are skipped, while every inner parenthesis is kept. For example, `"(()())"` becomes `"()()"`, and `"()()"` becomes `""`. The solution runs in **O(n)** time with a single pass and uses only the output string as extra space.
